condition: mild fine white scalp flaking 2 weeks after starting daily hot water hair washing
level_rationale: Noticing fine white flakes across the scalp today 2 weeks after starting daily hot-water hair washing in a 31-year-old adult reflects uncomplicated superficial scalp dryness or flaking appropriate for over-the-counter moisturizing scalp lotion self-care, whereas raw weeping open sores across the scalp require an outpatient doctor examination for exudative or secondarily infected scalp dermatosis rather than cosmetic self-care lotion.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic facts (age 31, starting daily hot-water hair washing 2 weeks ago, and fine white scalp flakes today) with no diagnosis label or dialect lexicon term in any text and an exact 1-word vs 1-word span swap. Replacing only fact f3 ('fine white flakes' to 'raw weeping open sores') stays on the exact scalp surface in the same patient and shifts care from over-the-counter moisturizing lotion (level 1) to outpatient physician evaluation (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5 and Rules A and D) with zero stated negatives.
